role.altitude: The preschool special education teacher keeps observing, judging, reading aloud, guiding children with equipment and talking with parents and specialists; looking up a child's goals and earlier notes, finding suitable books and props, and arranging meetings shrink a little.
skills_to_grow: Using the child overview before conversations
role.ambitious_version: A teacher who walks into every plan meeting with the child's full picture already on one page.

tasks.short: Look up the child's goals and earlier observations, observe and evaluate students' performance, behavior, social development and physical health.

steps.what: Teacher looks up the child's plan goals and earlier observations
Teacher observes students' performance, behavior, social development and physical health
Teacher evaluates the child's development against the goals

tasks.design: A child overview in the pupil record shows plan goals, recent observations and therapist notes on one screen, instead of opening several documents. Observing and evaluating stay fully with the teacher; no software assesses the child. Writing observations down belongs to the records task and is priced there.
tasks.previous_blocker: Goals and notes sat in separate documents.
tasks.still_hard: Children whose signals are hard to read.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing a small step forward in a child who rarely speaks.

evidence.claim: A pupil record system has a support plan module and goal tracking.
AI that evaluates learning outcomes is high-risk; here the teacher evaluates.

assumptions: Boundary: observing and evaluating; keeping records (task 19093) and testing development levels (task 19087) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s1: goals and notes kept in the pupil record by the teacher and therapists.
Observing and evaluating keep their full time.
unknowns: Whether therapists write in the same record.
research_questions: Do evaluations refer to plan goals more often?

incremental.description: Teacher asks therapists to add notes to the shared record.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few children with plans; high: a group where every child has detailed goals.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Choose books for the group, prepare picture supports and props, and read books to entire classes or small groups.

steps.what: Teacher chooses books that suit the group's level and needs
Teacher prepares picture supports and props for the story
Teacher reads books to entire classes or small groups, with signs and pictures

tasks.design: The school's book collection is listed with level, topic and available picture supports, so the teacher finds suitable books faster, and picture sets for common books are kept in a shared folder to print. Reading aloud stays fully with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supports were made again for each book.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared catalogues and picture set folders.
tasks.still_hard: Children with very different needs in one group.
tasks.human_edge: Keeping a restless child with the story.

reach.learn: Whether shared picture sets get reused.

evidence.claim: Shared catalogues and material folders save looking up and remaking materials.

assumptions: Boundary: reading to children; teaching basic skills (task 19084) is a sibling task.
research_questions: Are picture sets reused across groups?

incremental.description: Teacher adds new picture sets to the shared folder.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a small familiar collection; high: frequent new books with supports.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Gather reports and observations, schedule the meeting, confer with parents, administrators, testing specialists and social workers to develop individual education plans, and answer follow-up questions.

steps.what: Teacher gathers specialist reports, test results and observations before the meeting
Teacher schedules the meeting with parents and specialists
Teacher confers with parents, administrators, testing specialists and social workers to develop the individual education plan
Teacher answers follow-up questions from parents and specialists

tasks.design: Specialist reports, test results and recent observations are attached to the child's record, so the teacher reads one overview before the meeting instead of collecting files from mail. A scheduling poll finds a time for parents and specialists. Conferring and answering questions stay fully personal. Writing the plan document belongs to the plan development task and is priced there.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reports arrived by mail and meetings took many messages to arrange.
tasks.enabler_now: Pupil records with attached reports and scheduling polls.
tasks.still_hard: Parents and professionals who disagree about the child.
tasks.human_edge: Helping parents feel heard while agreeing realistic goals.
tasks.altitude: Less preparation and arranging; the meeting stays.

evidence.claim: A support plan is set within six weeks of enrolment after consulting parents and evaluated yearly.
Parents and staff must consent to rules on pupil data and to tools that can monitor staff.

assumptions: Boundary: conferring on plans; writing plans (task 19067) and keeping records (task 19093) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s1: specialists upload their reports to the child's record, about 70% of reports; s1 is priced at that share.
Conferring and follow-up keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of specialists with record access.
research_questions: Are plans agreed within the legal deadline more often?

incremental.description: Teacher arranges record access for new specialists.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few specialists with record access; high: 70% of reports in the record.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Instruct and monitor students in the use and care of equipment or materials, and check equipment after use.

steps.what: Teacher instructs students in the use and care of equipment and materials
Teacher monitors students using equipment to prevent injuries and damage
Teacher checks equipment after use and reports damage

tasks.design: Instructing and monitoring stay fully in the room. Damage is reported with a short form on the classroom tablet that goes straight to the caretaker, instead of a note or a hallway conversation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Nothing blocked it; this is teaching.
tasks.still_hard: Children who cannot yet understand danger.
tasks.human_edge: Stepping in a second before a child gets hurt.

evidence.claim: Short report forms replace notes for routine requests.

assumptions: Boundary: teaching safe use of equipment; managing inventory (task 19091) is a sibling task.
Instructing and monitoring keep their full time.

incremental.description: Teacher learns the damage report form.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: little equipment; high: many tools and devices in daily use.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
